layers.identification: Single-storey timber cottage with a front-facing gable, raised porch, and stone chimney; primaryDomain=building.
layers.formSilhouette: 6.0 m front span by 7.5 m depth; 2.4 m eave-wall height on a 0.45 m stone plinth; symmetric gable rises to a 5.4 m total height; long dark pitched roof projects beyond every wall.
layers.macroMesoMicro: Macro: plinth, timber shell, gable roof, porch, chimney. Meso: horizontal siding, fascia, porch canopy, posts, rails, steps, doors, framed windows, chimney cap. Micro: roof shingle courses, sill strips, muntins, balusters, stone courses and lantern proxy.
layers.spatialRelationships: The walls sit flush on the plinth; gable triangles continue the end walls; roof planes overlap the gables and walls; chimney penetrates the rear-right roof plane; porch deck overlaps the front wall and steps meet grade; posts connect deck to canopy.
layers.materialsSurface: Warm sealed cedar has horizontal board relief and medium roughness; plinth and chimney are cool grey irregular stone; roof is charcoal asphalt shingle with high roughness; glass is dark desaturated blue-grey; metal lantern is near-black.
layers.colorFinish: Cedar base #A97849 with darker trim #633F24; stone #66625B; roof #292725; glass #344450; metal #16191A. Wood roughness 0.45-0.6, stone 0.75-0.9, roof 0.75-0.85, glass 0.08-0.18.
layers.identityFeatures: Centered panel door, paired front windows, small gable window, continuous porch railing, three-step entry, deep eaves with fascia, visible dark roof courses and a rectangular stone chimney with cap.
layers.uncertainty: The reference omits the exact back/underside construction and stone pattern. The graph will infer symmetric gable treatment, a rear window, and procedural rectangular stone/shingle courses.

observation.shapeAnalysis: CreateBoxMesh is used for rectilinear shell, boards, frames, porch and stone modules; the gable is a closed triangular cross-section swept across the end-wall thickness; roof planes are thin rotated boxes; every hard-surface part receives its own bevel before a module merge.
observation.note: Fill every layer from the reference BEFORE authoring. This prose is the durable memory of the reference; the conversation attachment is not.

visualTokens.note: Distill hex colors, roughness/metalness ranges, and key ratios so material and final-acceptance stages consult data instead of recalling the image.

objectClass.notes: Local front axis is +Z. The authoring target is a modular web-ready building generator rather than a static illustration.

definitionOfDone: Match the 6.0m by 7.5m one-storey cedar cabin with a 5.4m front gable silhouette at front and three-quarter views.
Include a raised stone plinth, connected porch deck and steps, canopy posts/rails, deep eaves, chimney, door, gable window, two front windows and side/rear windows.
Represent at least 16 reference-defining meso/micro details as actual PCG nodes: siding courses, roof courses, stone courses, fascia, muntins, sill strips, balusters and chimney cap.
Use authored named material slots with UV projection for wood, dark trim, stone, roof, glass and metal; no default material output remains.
Every support, roof, chimney, porch and wall contact overlaps by a small physically plausible tolerance; no visible floating assemblies.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate identity-defining details; each must mapsTo a real node id/property, never prose only.

modules.role: pitched planes, gables, fascia, shingle courses and chimney
deck, canopy, posts, rails, balusters and stairs
door panels, framed/mullioned windows, sills and lantern

unknownsToResolve: Exact rear opening placement is inferred as a centered lower window.
Stone and shingle variation use procedural rows instead of copying the 2D drawing texture.

acceptance: Module table recorded (nameable parts, Subgraph yes/no)
Macro parts present as node chains or Subgraph stubs
Render or SceneView screenshot for silhouette review
No floating parts without TransformMesh placement
Bevel amounts scaled to each part (not one post-merge amount)
Lane layout / Subgraph packaging if soft triggers fire
AssignMaterial / VertexColor / UV on named parts
Identity finish zones mapped (not flat memory colors)
parameters[] synced with target node data defaults
recommended Graph Parameters auto-applied when signals fire (or [] / user-listed)

authoringInstruction: Fill objectClass, qualityContract, detailInventory, and modules from the reference before writing .pcg nodes. Use report_pass.py for the next command.
